18.0.s.en: (1) The friendship of Jonathan with David

18.0.0.en: Jonathan, the son of Saul, was present at the conversation between Saul his father and David after the battle, and Jonathan loved David greatly; to express the intensity of this love, it is said that he loved him as his own soul. The friendship of Jonathan and David became strong because its conditions were present in both of them, namely:

18.0.1.en: 1- They had one goal, which was the love of God and zeal for His name, which appeared in Jonathan's challenge of the Philistines and David's fight against Goliath.

18.0.2.en: 2- They were alike in strong faith in God, which gave them rare courage against the enemies.

18.0.3.en: 3- Each was ready to sacrifice himself for the other, as would appear in Jonathan's defense of David before his father, when Saul was enraged and rose up to kill his son.

18.1.0.en: As for Saul the king, who also loved David greatly and became attached to him, he did not let him return again to Bethlehem but kept him with his men.

18.2.0.en: As for Jonathan, he expressed his love for David by making a covenant with him to be his friend to the end of his life, and indeed both of them kept their covenant; indeed, the friendship of Jonathan and David became an example for all generations.

18.3.2.en: As a sign of the covenant between the two friends, Jonathan gave a token to his friend David: he took off his own "robe" and gave it to David as a gift, and he also gave his sword, his bow and his leather belt. These are all things very personal to a man, and it is not easy to part with them, but he did this with all love, as if he were giving the dearest thing he had to his new friend.

18.4.0.en: The Lord gave David favor in the eyes of Saul, since the Lord was with David and he prospered in all the tasks the king assigned to him. Therefore Saul gave him a high position in his army, and he became one of the commanders of war. God blessed David even more, and he became beloved by all the servants of Saul and also by all the people of Israel.

18.4.1.en: If you live in godliness and hold fast to God's commandments, He will give you favor in the eyes of others, so that they love you and you live in good relationships with them, which helps you to succeed in your life and also in serving others and drawing them to Christ.

18.5.0.en: Saul's love for David did not last long, for some events came that turned everything upside down. After a period of time, when Saul decided to return from the places of war and enter the cities of the people, as was the custom with victorious kings, the people came out to meet them. And indeed the women came out to meet the victorious men, with musical instruments such as timbrels and ringing triangles, and they danced and chanted with singing.

18.6.1.en: There were always popular poems and songs sung on such occasions and celebrations, so the dancing women began to chant: Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands. Of course, the women did not intend to provoke Saul, but the words came out this way as an expression of their recognition of David's merit in this great victory over Goliath and the Philistines.

18.7.0.en: Saul was greatly angered, because of his human jealousy, by the words of the women, and he considered it a kind of insolence and a belittling of himself, and he said, They have ascribed to me thousands and to David they have ascribed ten thousands, so what more can he have but the kingdom? That is, nothing remains but that David should also take the kingdom from me and the rule should become his!!!

18.8.0.en: After these events Saul began to harbor evil against David, and his former love turned into hatred, jealousy and a desire to be rid of him.

18.8.1.en: Do not be troubled if they praise another person in your presence and do not praise you; this does not mean that you are belittled. Be positive and learn from the virtues of those they praise, and be content with pleasing God, for He is better than every human praise.

18.9.0.en: As at other times (literally, as day by day): an expression meaning from time to time.

18.9.1.en: On the day after Saul's anger at the chanting of the women, a state of agitation came upon him because of the unclean spirit, and as usual they brought David, the lute player, who began to play. Satan (the unclean spirit) exploited Saul's hatred of David and his jealousy of him and drove him to kill David, especially since he was holding his spear. So Saul hurled the spear toward David, who was leaning against the wall, and tried to kill him, but David was able to escape from Saul twice, and the spear struck the wall and did not hit David.

18.9.2.en: Here we find Saul the king, in whose hand was all authority, fearing David, envying him and trying to kill him, while David flees from before him and God preserves him from all the plots of Saul. From this we conclude how great was Saul's inner weakness, because he was not with God even though he had the authority of a king, whereas David, who seemed to have no authority, had all power with him because God was with him.

18.10.0.en: This verse reveals to us that although Saul was still the king and David was merely one of his servants, God's departure from Saul and His strengthening of David made it Saul who feared David.

18.10.1.en: This teaches us, beloved, to acquire the fear of God and His love, and to obtain His favor toward us, for if the Lord is with us, who can be against us... God gives awe and inner strength, so that no one can frighten you or terrify your heart, but He makes all your enemies fear you.

18.11.0.en: As cunning politicians do, so Saul did with David. He could not harm the hero of the people or kill him, so he gave him a position of honor and limited authority, but kept him away from himself and from his court and made him captain over a thousand. David was faithful in his work, and the Lord gave him success and strengthened him, and he became beloved by all the people.

18.12.0.en: The news of David's success reached Saul, and his fear of him increased even more, for he had come to stand as the foremost man of the people, since everyone loved him, from his own tribe and from all the tribes of the people. For the people love the leader who mingles with them and lives among them, like Christ, who lived in the midst of the crowds and suffered their sufferings (Heb 2:17).

18.13.0.en: Jealousy grew greatly in Saul's heart with David's success and the people's love for him, so a very cunning idea went around in his mind for getting rid of him and killing him: to offer him a great honor, namely giving him his elder daughter "Merab" in marriage, on condition that David be the commander of his army in fighting the Philistines. Thus David would be exposed to death in these wars and would be killed by the hand of the Philistines, while Saul's hand would remain clean of his blood. Here we see David's humility: he did not demand his right to marry the king's daughter without a dowry, for he had already paid it by killing Goliath, since Saul had promised this, but he obeyed.

18.14.0.en: In humility and self-denial, David answered Saul that he was not worthy of this noble kinship, saying, Who am I, and what is my family, that I should be worthy of becoming the king's son-in-law?

18.15.0.en: At the time set for the marriage, we are surprised that Saul's daughter was given to another man, unknown, from the town of "Meholah" in the Jordan valley, named "Adriel". We do not know the reason for this change; perhaps Saul broke his promise in order to vex and humiliate David among the people. We see here that while Saul breaks his promise to David and does not give him Merab, God rewards him with many rewards, which are:

18.15.1.en: 1- Success in his wars with the Philistines, so that he appeared as a great warrior leader.

18.15.2.en: 2- The friendship of Jonathan, the son of Saul, toward him.

18.15.3.en: 3- The love of Michal for him, which would stand with him against her father, as will appear later.

18.15.4.en: 4- The love of the people and their rallying around him.

18.16.0.en: On the other hand, after the marriage of "Merab", "Michal", the younger daughter of Saul, loved David, and when Saul's men learned of it they told him, and he welcomed the matter greatly.

18.17.0.en: A snare: a trap and a net.

18.17.1.en: Michal's declaration of her love for David came in keeping with what Saul had previously prepared in his heart to be rid of him at the hands of the Philistines, so he offered David kinship by marriage and the wedding.

18.18.0.en: Saul's speech to David was not direct but through the men of his court, since it was not proper for the king to offer his daughter to David himself. Indeed the men went and spoke to David to encourage him toward the idea of becoming the king's son-in-law, the king who loved him and preferred him over the rest of the men. When the men spoke such kind words to David, he answered them that it was not easy for a man like him to become son-in-law to the daughter of the king of Israel, since he was a poor man and not one of the wealthy of the people.

18.19.0.en: Foreskins: the male genital part, uncircumcised.

18.19.1.en: The men carried everything David had said to Saul, and Saul seized the opportunity to be rid of David. He sent David a message through his men, saying that he did not care about money as a dowry for his daughter, but wanted David to bring a hundred foreskins of the Philistines as the dowry for Michal. Saul's purpose was that David would fight the Philistines and die in the war, and so he would be rid of him.

18.20.0.en: The king's men informed David of the king's request, and because David was courageous, the word pleased him and he made light of the task. He gathered his men, and before the time set by Saul for accomplishing this task had ended, David, trusting in God, was able to attack the Philistines and kill two hundred men, that is, twice the number Saul had asked for, and he brought their foreskins to Saul. This was the dowry of Michal, with which David married her.

18.21.0.en: After these events Saul became sure that God supported David in all his affairs, and his daughter Michal was also attached to David, so Saul's anger, jealousy and fear of David increased, and Saul's enmity toward David grew.

18.22.0.en: The princes of the Philistines began to go out and attack the people of God again and again, but each time they went out God gave victory to the people of God. David and his men were more successful and distinguished in these wars, so that the name of David was greatly loved and revered among all the people.

18.22.1.en: Although the Law provides that a bridegroom is exempt from war for a year (Deut 24:5), David gave up his right in order to defend his country and fight the Philistines.

18.22.2.en: We see through the events of this chapter how evil Saul's heart was and how all his schemes were to be rid of David, and we also see how God turned evil into good, and all things led to the exaltation of David's name among the people in preparation for his becoming king. This reminds us of what Joseph said to his brothers, that they meant evil against him, but God turned the evil and used it for the good and blessing of Joseph (Gen 50:20). So make your heart steadfast and leave it to God to deal with all the plots of evil around you, even if threats and plots surround you, for God is able to turn them to your good and to protect you in all your steps as long as you hold fast to His commandments. Saul's attempts to kill David

19.0.s.en: (1) Saul's order to kill David and the success of Jonathan's intercession

19.0.0.en: After Saul had been planning secretly within himself to be rid of "David", he could not keep the matter hidden within himself, especially after David's successive successes, and so he declared to his son Jonathan, and also to the officers of his army who were close to him, his desire to kill "David!"

19.1.0.en: But God, who protects those who trust in Him, put a wonderful love in Jonathan's heart toward David, so Jonathan hastened to tell David what Saul wanted to do and advised him to hide so as to be safe from his father and his men. Jonathan did not try to push David to flee altogether from the face of Saul his father, because he loved him and wanted the kingdom to benefit from him as a military commander; he had hope of calming his father toward him so that he would treat him kindly, but when he despaired of this, he encouraged him to flee, as will appear later.

19.2.0.en: Jonathan also told David that he would go with his father to one of the fields, where he would speak with him, trying to dissuade him from his intention to kill David, and Jonathan agreed to inform David of the result of his conversation with his father.

19.3.0.en: This conversation took place, of course, in one of the fields, as we understood from the previous verse. Jonathan began his words to Saul his father by saying that "David" had not sinned against Saul for even one day; on the contrary, all his works had been good in the eyes of the people and in your eyes too, for he risked his life and went to kill "Goliath", whom all the men feared, and so he was an instrument of God's salvation for His people. You yourself saw it and rejoiced over the man, so why do you commit today this great sin and sin against God and against your own reputation by killing this man without cause?

19.4.0.en: The Lord gave grace to Jonathan's words in the heart of his father Saul, and the king responded and swore to his son by the name of the living God that he would not kill David or do him harm.

19.5.0.en: Jonathan hastened to David's hiding place and told him the whole of the previous conversation with his father and how it ended, and he brought David with him to meet Saul. David was before Saul as before, beloved by him and in his service.

19.6.0.en: When the Philistines again tried to attack the children of Israel, David and his men went out against them and defeated them, and they all fled from before him, and David sang his fifty-ninth psalm.

19.6.1.en: May you defend the oppressed if you have the opportunity, even if you bear some blame from people or lose anything. Put yourself in the place of the oppressed so that you feel for him and defend him, and know that God has defended you, who were oppressed and condemned to death because of the sin into which the devil made you fall, and He died for you and redeemed you... So from today take an interest in every oppressed person whom you can defend or to whom you can render a service.

19.7.s.en: (2) New attempts to kill David and his escape from them

19.7.0.en: These two verses are the same scene that happened in (ch. 16:14), of the unclean spirit suddenly seizing Saul and his attempt to kill David (ch. 18:11), and David was able to escape.

19.8.0.en: We find that Saul had returned to his evil nature and began again to plan to be rid of "David". He ordered some men to watch him all night and to kill him when the sun appeared, but some men loyal to David learned of the matter and informed "Michal", his wife, who in turn warned David to flee from his house that very night or he would be killed in the morning. Indeed David heeded the advice of his wife, who was able to smuggle him out through a window of the house. David began a journey of fleeing from place to place before the pursuits of Saul, and he had no fixed dwelling place until the death of Saul; in this he is a type of Christ, who had nowhere to lay His head.

19.9.0.en: Teraphim: the image of an idol, or small figures that people kept to bring good luck. After Michal was assured of her husband's escape, she came up with a new trick: she placed in the place of David's bed an image the size of a man, put under its head a piece of goat's skin as a pillow, and covered it with a garment as a kind of disguise.

19.9.1.en: Michal's keeping of idol figures is a strange thing that shows her heart was not upright toward God. She certainly kept these figures without David's knowledge, and perhaps she wished that these figures would grant her offspring.

19.10.0.en: Saul learned that "David" had not gone out in the morning as usual and that the men had not been able to kill him, so he sent his men to seek David that he might come down to him. As for Michal, in order to use up time and give her husband a greater chance to escape, she sent the men back to her father with the excuse that he was sick and could not leave his bed.

19.11.0.en: Saul's anger grew very strong, so he sent his men again to David's house, commanding them to bring him even if he were very sick, that he might carry out his evil counsel of killing him. When the men broke into his house, they found in the bed nothing but the image and the goat's skin at its head.

19.12.0.en: When the matter was uncovered, Saul reproached his daughter for deceiving him and smuggling out her husband, and she gave him an answer that would save her from his anger and revenge, namely that she had done so under David's pressure and his threat to kill her.

19.12.1.en: Believe in God, who is able to protect you however much the wicked try to harm you, for He gives you favor in the eyes of some of those around you and moves circumstances so that you escape from evil, and so the power of God appears, and you thank Him and live your life to glorify His holy name.

19.13.s.en: (3) David's refuge with Samuel and Saul's continuing attempts

19.13.0.en: Naioth: located on the outskirts of Ramah, and Samuel made it the seat of a school of the prophets; perhaps David learned there at the hands of Samuel.

19.13.1.en: When David fled, leaving his house, he headed for Ramah and stayed where Samuel lived, and as soon as he found him he told him all that Saul had done to him and how he was planning to kill him. So Samuel took him to "Naioth" and settled him there.

19.13.2.en: How good it is for a person in his distress to take refuge in his father of confession, to hear the voice of God and to keep away from evil.

19.14.1.en: Saul learned of David's hiding place with Samuel in "Naioth", so he sent some of his men to arrest him. But when these messengers arrived at "Naioth" they found the company of the prophets praising God, with Samuel the prophet leading them in it, and instead of arresting David a spiritual state took hold of them and the Holy Spirit moved them, so they joined the prophets in what they were doing and began to praise God themselves also. That is, the Holy Spirit came upon the messengers and changed them from a state of evil and vengeance against David to a calm spiritual thought, namely the praise of God.

19.15.0.en: Saul learned what had happened to his men whom he had sent, so he sent a second group to bring David, and the Spirit of God, the Holy, came upon them and they did as their predecessors had done; and he sent also a third group, and they too prophesied.

19.16.0.en: Sechu: located north of Ramah, at a distance of 5 km.

19.16.1.en: Saul's patience ran out after the many missions he had sent to bring David, so he decided to go himself. Before reaching Ramah he stopped at "Sechu", beside a well known and great well in it, and asked more carefully about the place of Samuel and David, and the people told him that they were in "Naioth."

19.17.0.en: Saul went on the road to Ramah and Naioth, but on the road, before he arrived, the Spirit of God came upon him, and he too began to praise God as he was on his way there.

19.17.1.en: We find that God was calling Saul to repentance and to casting out jealousy, envy and the attempt to kill David, and He warned him of this in many ways:

19.17.2.en: 1- Jonathan's intercession and his attempt to turn him back from his hatred.

19.17.3.en: 2- Michal's smuggling out of David and her support for him.

19.17.4.en: 3- The prophesying of Saul's messengers, and then his own prophesying when he tried to arrest him at Naioth.

19.17.5.en: 4- The attack of the Philistines on the land of the Jews while he was pursuing David, so that he was forced to leave him and go to fight them (ch. 23:27).

19.17.6.en: 5- His falling twice into David's hand, but David forgave him and let him go (ch. 24, ch. 26).

19.18.0.en: When Saul arrived at "Naioth", the Spirit of the Lord worked in him even more, so he humbled himself and took off all the garments of the king and also his military dress, and remained in his undergarments, and he went on praising God all day and night, until he fell and lay prostrate from exhaustion. The people marveled and said, after they had seen him... Is Saul also among the prophets?! This last saying, however, became a proverb used in mockery of a person who may do a great deed that people do not expect of him.

19.18.1.en: We note that this is the second time Saul prophesied, for he prophesied on a previous occasion after he was anointed king (ch. 10:10). Thus God turned Saul's heart to calm concerning David, and he began to prophesy the word of God, but because of Saul's persistence in pride he returned again to hating David and trying to kill him.

19.18.2.en: It is mentioned in (ch. 15:35) that Samuel would not come again to see Saul, yet he saw him here. If we look closely we find that Saul did not come to take counsel from Samuel, and that is what Samuel meant, that he would not meet Saul again in order to counsel him. What happened this time is that Saul came to search for David and saw Samuel, but not with the purpose of benefiting from Samuel.

19.18.3.en: God prevented Saul from killing David as a protection for David and to keep Saul from falling into sin, so He turned his heart to prophesying instead of evil and killing.

19.18.4.en: May you pay attention to God's attempts to keep you from evil and seize these opportunities for repentance, for they are love from God, who seeks your repentance, because if you do not do this you are exposed to destruction in the end, as happened with Saul. Jonathan's covenant with David and his defense of him before Saul
